subject: CAIQ: Clarify deployment affinity scope and evidence collection
messages:
From: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@greenridgehealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: audits@cloudassure.io
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ follow-up: deployment affinity / tenant boundary evidence

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the initial CAIQ submission last month. Our security team at GreenRidge has one clarifying ask before we sign off on the deployment-affinity controls: we need explicit evidence showing how tenant affinity is enforced at runtime (not just in architecture diagrams). Specifically:

- A short explanation of how workloads are pinned (or not pinned) to dedicated GPU pools per-tenant
- Sample logs or traces that demonstrate a tenant-scoped serving request and the KV cache lifecycle for a single inference session
- Any existing integration tests or post-deploy checks you run to confirm tenant isolation between customers

Can you point us to artifacts (logs, CI test output, or a summarized runbook) that prove these controls are operating? We prefer artifacts that are consumable by our auditors rather than just high-level descriptions.

If you need to loop in someone on the runtime or infra team, please do — we want this closed in the next two weeks to meet our procurement schedule.

Thanks,
Andrew Mills
Senior InfoSec Manager
GreenRidge Health

Hi Andrew —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers up front:

- Tenant affinity: Redwood supports both "shared" and "dedicated" deployment modes. For Dedicated pools we pin inference workloads to reserved GPU nodes by affinity labels; for Shared we rely on strict runtime multi-tenancy plus per-tenant namespace enforcement.
- Evidence types we can provide: deployment topology diagram, sample request-to-response trace showing tenant identifiers being honored (redacted), KV cache lifecycle excerpt for a single session, and our tenant isolation test summary.

I don’t want to send raw logs over email — I will stage redacted samples to a secured Drive folder and attach a short narrative mapping each artifact to the CAIQ control.

Marissa / Kimberly — can one of you pull the KV cache excerpt and the tenant-isolation test report (redact PII), and add them to the Drive folder listed below? Jonas, can you confirm the affinity labels and provide a one-paragraph note on how shard/pool pinning is implemented?

Timeline: we can share the Drive package by tomorrow EOD and a short executive summary by Tuesday. Does that work for GreenRidge auditors?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference
